First of all, I have to say that Professor Malesevic is a highly knowledgeable, passionate, and well-equipped academic in his field. I genuinely feel that I walked away from each class learning something valuable.
That said, HCIV102 is clearly designed to be an introductory and general requirement course. I’m not sure whether Professor Malesevic was aware of this fact, but to me, it didn’t quite feel like he was. Speaking for myself, I don’t have a particular interest in history. I’m only taking this course because it’s mandatory. And I doubt that anyone who is truly passionate about history would choose HCIV102 as a platform to explore it deeply. Most of us are simply trying to fulfill a graduation requirement. None of us are MA level history students, yet I felt that the expectations, particularly in terms of essay performance, were on that level. Otherwise, the grading seems hard to make sense of.
It was honestly disheartening to be expected to meet such high standards, including the implicit expectation to engage with Ancient Greek and Latin texts??? within just two months. We’re sorry if we failed to meet those expectations. I don’t know, perhaps we just have very different views on what university is meant to be. For better or worse, many students today see university as a stepping stone to better job opportunities. That’s the reality for most. I'm not sure how many students at Bilkent would consider learning French just to read La Révolution in its original language for an HCIV102 midterm essay. And if there is such a student, they’re probably not enrolled in this course in the first place. To be clear, Professor Malesevic is an excellent instructor. But it might be helpful if he could better align his expectations with the actual student profile of this course. Otherwise, I wouldn’t recommend taking this course with him unless you’re ready to start brushing up on your Latin (?) well in advance.
